A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D. Text comparison and visual inspection support a reliable assessment.

before.justification: v3 reports original LLM comparisons, KG perturbation experiments, human/LLM evaluation studies and multilingual results in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Table 2, Figures 4–6 and the appendix evaluation and multilingual studies.

M1.justification: The query-generation procedure, PPR pruning, prize-cost retrieval variants and graph-guided generation remain unchanged. Rewriting the path-retrieval explanation in Appendix A.3 does not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain DBpedia-based OKGQA and OKGQA-P, the same query categories and perturbation scenarios, and the five-language KG-context experiment in Appendix B.1. Dataset statistics and coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains identical model-by-comparator membership for zero-shot and four-shot prompting, CoT, CoT+SC, Wikipedia-based IRCoT and KG retrieval variants. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The detailed protocols retain the same backbones, metrics, prompts, graph extraction settings and appendix sample sizes. Section 4.1 newly discloses decoding parameters; it does not revise previously specified values or establish that experiments changed.

E4.justification: The four KG perturbation analyses, query-construction validation, evaluator agreement checks and query–DBpedia alignment analysis were already present in v3. v4 retains their questions and evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same ± reporting in Tables 2 and 5 and the same Pearson correlation and Cohen’s kappa analyses. No repeated-run counts, seeds or uncertainty-estimation procedures are newly reported or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 2–6 retain identical values, and Figures 4–6 retain the same plotted results. The human–LLM correlation of 0.78 and Appendix B.2 alignment statistics are also unchanged. Changes to table boldface affect presentation rather than numerical rankings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, prize-cost scoring expressions, perturbation definitions and the ATS, SC2D and SD2 definitions in Appendix A.5 are retained. No substantive mathematical revision or new proof appears.

C1.justification: The OKGQA/OKGQA-P contributions and main findings retain their meaning: KG information reduces factual errors, internal reasoning alone can hallucinate, subgraphs benefit simpler queries, and KG benefits can persist under contamination. The rewritten abstract and introduction do not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: The interpretations of retrieval performance, perturbation sensitivity, evaluator reliability and multilingual context remain substantively unchanged. Both versions retain the limitations concerning DBpedia coverage and static knowledge graphs.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly specifies temperature = 0.7 and top_p = 1.0 for all models and identifies OpenAI and OpenRouter API services. The code/data footnote replaces the anonymous address with the named Y-Sui/OKGQA GitHub repository. These are documentation and access-information changes.

R1.justification: v4 adds contextual citations to Chen et al. (2025) on indirect prompt injection, He et al. (2025) on UniGraph2 and Sui (2021) on tourism KG question answering. The existing research positioning remains largely unchanged; bibliographic updates to retained works do not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: Extensive rewriting covers the abstract and most of the introduction, with further paragraph revisions in dataset construction and Appendices A.1, A.3 and A.4. The section hierarchy remains intact. Editorial changes also introduce malformed bibliography entries and misleadingly describe the human evaluators as 'LLM evaluators' in the A.1 overview.

P2.justification: All eight figures and seven tables are retained. v4 enlarges Table 2 and changes its boldface emphasis, moves Figure 7 between columns, and places Table 6 after its accompanying discussion. Caption, spacing and hyperlink-color changes are limited presentation revisions.

improvement.justification: v4 improves reproducibility documentation through explicit decoding settings and API-provider information, and makes Table 2 more readable. However, it introduces malformed reference years and truncated identifiers, plus misleading evaluator terminology in Appendix A.1. With the scientific evidence unchanged, the net direction is uncertain because these documentation gains coexist with losses in bibliographic accuracy and explanatory consistency.
